videos.title: Ladipoe On REVIVAL Album, 8-Year Wait & “Road Rage” Transition | Cool FM Interview
videos.headline: Ladipoe On REVIVAL Album, 8-Year Wait & “Road Rage” Transition | Cool FM Interview
videos.description:
Ladipoe (Leader of the Revival) sits with KemiSmallz and Brownish on Cool FM’s Midday Show to talk the long-awaited sophomore album REVIVAL.

He explains what “Revival” really means to him, why the project took eight years to drop, the thematic link between “Road Rage” and “Old Ways,” the exclusive radio version of “No Level,” his writing process and word choices, biblical references in his music, the vulnerable story behind “Palm Trees” and “One More Time,” meeting Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala at the AI For Good Summit in Geneva, acting in Christmas in Lagos, and more.

Topics include:
•  The meaning of Revival and “Leader of the Revival”
•  Apology to the Lifelines for the wait
•  How “Road Rage” phases into “Old Ways”
•  Choosing vocalists and features
•  Unlearning perfection
•  Nigerian hip-hop and carrying the culture
•  Family, faith, and the humanity behind the music
•  Games, books, bikes, and life outside the booth
Stream REVIVAL now.

Subscribe to Cool FM Nigeria for more interviews.

 #Afrobeats 
#HipHopNigeria

videos.title: “Burna Boy Is a Huge Inspiration to My Sound” — Buff Opens Up on His Music, 10 Minutes & More
videos.headline: “Burna Boy Is a Huge Inspiration to My Sound” — Buff Opens Up on His Music, 10 Minutes & More
videos.description:
In this exclusive full interview on the Midday Show with Kemi Smalls and Brownish on 96.9 Cool FM, Nigerian artist 6uff (Buff / 6uffzaddy) opens up about his music journey, gym lifestyle, personality, and more.

From church drummer and producer (as Logic) to breakthrough artist, 6uff shares how he started making music in 2021 with “Selfish,” the story behind his stage name, and the impact of family support — especially his mom’s prayers.

He talks about his breakout tracks **Prodigy** and **Idi Amin**, the massive collaboration **10 Minutes** with Odumodublvck, **Ripper’s Fate** with Tuff King, his heavy bass signature sound, perfectionism in the studio, and upcoming projects (including possible links with Burna Boy and Rondtown).

Also covered:

- His 6’5” height and gym dedication (started with homemade cement weights)
- Ambivert personality vs high-energy stage presence and shirtless performances
- Football background (defensive midfield, Barcelona fan)
- Fitness advice, real-life song themes (betrayal, survival, hustle)
- Guilty pleasures, movie preferences, and dream Nigerian cypher line-up

Stream 6uff’s music:  
• 10 Minutes (with Odumodublvck)  
• Prodigy  
• Ripper’s Fate (with Tuff King)  
• And more

videos.title: CKay Speaks on Banga Boy Album, Phyno Collab & Music as a Diary | Cool FM Interview
videos.headline: CKay Speaks on Banga Boy Album, Phyno Collab & Music as a Diary | Cool FM Interview
videos.description:
CKay sits down for an exclusive interview on Cool FM’s The Roadshow to discuss his new album Banga Boy

In this conversation, the “Love Nwantiti” star opens up about:  
• Why he named the project Banga Boy and the era he’s in right now  
• The album’s storyline — starting with a breakup, moving through club nights and healing  
• How the Phyno collaboration on “Para” started with a chance meeting at Houston Airport  
• Treating music like a public diary entry and staying true to real experiences  
• Side A vs Side B structure inspired by vinyl records  
• Producing tracks like NDA and Shege, and choosing features with the right energy (Mavo, King Promise & more)  
• Why chasing “international” sound isn’t the goal — feelings and vibes cross borders

CKay also shares insights on vulnerability (especially the last track “Bye Bye”), his self-taught production and music theory journey, and keeping a detached but grateful relationship with fan love. ‎
